hints: Every mirror piece has a centre. If you stand at a centre and step outwards one character at a time on both sides, when do you have to stop?
Use expand around centre: try all 2n−1 centres (each character, and each gap between two characters) and grow while the ends match.

1. For each index c, expand from (c, c) for odd lengths and from (c, c+1) for even lengths.
  2. While both ends are inside and equal, move them outward.
  3. The piece found is s[l+1 .. r-1]; if it is strictly longer than the best, remember its start and length.
  4. Return the best piece.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Check every substring for being a palindrome.

approaches.name: Optimal (for this size)
approaches.idea: Expand around each of the 2n−1 centres, keeping the longest piece.

explain: For "xabacdcx": centred on 'b' (index 2) we grow to aba (length 3). Centred on 'd' we grow to cdc, also length 3, but it starts later, so we keep aba. Because centres are tried left to right and we only replace on a strictly longer piece, ties go to the leftmost start. Remember even-length centres, or you will miss pieces like abba; and a string with no repeats returns its first character.
recognize: Longest palindromic substring → expand around every centre (odd and even).
